decisions.executionNote: Use left arm for the left-side basket; lift and begin turning fingers downward, keeping elbow-up continuity.
Advance above the back egg in the left basket while completing a vertical approach; reassess wrist alignment before descending.
Align the vertical fingertips with the back egg and lower slowly, leaving the gripper open until centered.
Finish the short descent around the back egg and close the left gripper; retention will be checked during a small lift.
Lift the first egg clear of the basket with the gripper kept closed; verify that it follows the fingers.
The egg is visibly retained. Carry it toward the left-back holder cup at clearance height, keeping the other arm parked.
Bring the retained egg over the back-left cup and begin the controlled descent, watching cup alignment.
The upright lid is obstructing the vertical wrist approach. Back away and incline the held egg toward the cup from the front-left to clear the lid.
An egg is now visible in the back-left cup and the fingers appear empty. Open and clear the holder toward the basket for the second egg.
Approach the leftmost remaining egg with the left fingers open and nearly vertical; the first egg remains visible in its cup.
Lower slowly around the second egg with a small centering correction, keeping the jaws open.
Close around the centered second egg, then lift gently to check retention without pushing farther into the basket.
The second egg was not retained and shifted toward the basket's left edge. Reopen and recenter over its new visible position.
The rim limits the outer jaw. Shift inward to center the egg between the fingers and use a narrower approach opening before grasping.
The egg is centered laterally; lower the fingertips to its midsection with a small forward adjustment, then close.
Lift the second egg straight clear while maintaining closure, checking visually that it follows the fingers.
The second egg is retained. Carry toward the holder while inclining the fingers so the wrist can stay in front of the open lid.
The second egg appears to have slipped during inclination. Stop the transfer, reopen, and return over its visible position to reassess after it settles.
Three eggs remain in the basket. Reapproach the back egg at its settled location, preserving the current near-vertical wrist orientation.
Center over the back egg and descend with open jaws to surround its body, rather than grasping only its tip.
Narrow the open approach to clear the rim, make a small centering descent, and close around the egg's wider middle.
Lift away from the rim without changing wrist angle, keeping the egg enclosed and checking visual retention.
The egg is visibly held. Translate toward the front-left cup without wrist rotation to avoid the previous slip and the upright lid.
Retention failed again. Reapproach the front egg instead, planning a deeper grasp around its body with a narrower opening to clear the basket rim.
Descend around the front egg with a slight leftward correction; keep the jaws open until they reach the egg's midsection.
Wrist view shows the egg forward and slightly right of the grasp center. Correct that offset before closing at the deeper height.
Test this grasp with a slow straight lift, keeping orientation and closure fixed; inspect whether the egg remains between the fingers.
The grasp was too far forward and shallow. Reopen, move back and left over the settled front egg, and lower to surround its middle before another closure.
The egg is now between the jaw faces. Close after a small lateral correction, then lift only a short distance to verify a stable grasp.
The egg is still in the basket. Reopen and adopt a straighter top-down approach to reduce rolling and improve grasp depth.
Lower another small amount to place the jaw faces around the egg's middle, then close gradually while holding the wrist stationary.
Test the deeper grasp with a slow vertical lift only; keep the fingers closed and avoid lateral acceleration.
Recenter from the head view and descend farther with open fingers; previous closures were not enclosing the egg securely.
At the deeper height, the wrist image shows the egg behind and right of the finger center. Recenter gently before attempting closure.
Bring the open jaw faces farther back and lower around the visible egg, then close while stationary for a fuller-body grasp.
Lift this centered grasp slowly straight upward while maintaining closure; check that the egg stays between the jaw faces.
The egg remains fixed between the jaws after lifting. Raise it clear of the rim without changing wrist angle before transferring.
Carry the securely held egg toward the front-left holder cup with gentle translation and unchanged orientation.
Continue the steady transfer over the empty front-left cup, maintaining the successful grasp and checking alignment before lowering.
Lower the held egg toward the front-left cup with a small rightward centering correction, keeping closure until it is seated.
Finish the short descent into the front-left cup, open to release the egg, and begin a gentle vertical withdrawal.
Two eggs are visibly in the holder. Withdraw upward and return toward the two remaining eggs in the basket.
Approach the nearer of the two remaining eggs from above, using the successful wrist angle and narrowing the open jaws to clear the rim.
Lower the open jaws straight around the nearer egg, retaining the angle that supported the previous successful grasp.
Center slightly right and lower to the successful grasp depth, then close gently around the nearer egg without moving laterally.
Test retention with a slow straight lift, holding the successful wrist angle and closed gripper.
The third egg remains between the fingers. Lift fully clear of the rim before carrying it toward the empty front-right cup.
Transfer the retained third egg steadily toward the holder at clearance height, keeping wrist orientation unchanged.
Move the egg over the front-right cup and start descending only after clearing the occupied left cups.
Lower the third egg over the front-right cup, correcting slightly left while preserving the grasp and keeping clear of the neighboring eggs.
Make the final small left-and-forward centering correction, release the third egg into the front-right cup, then lift clear.
Three eggs are seated in the holder. Lift clear of them and return toward the last egg in the left basket.
Approach the last egg at the back-right of the left basket, keeping the proven wrist angle and preparing a rim-clearing opening.
Use the wrist view to align left and forward over the last egg while lowering with the jaws open.
The last egg is aligned between the open fingers. Lower toward the successful grasp height while watching for rim interference.
Recenter the last egg between the jaw faces by moving slightly back and right, then close at the deeper grasp height.
The egg rolled back during closure and is still below the jaw center. Reopen and follow it back before attempting a more centered grasp.
Test the centered last-egg grasp with a slow vertical lift, maintaining closure and wrist angle.
The final egg remains retained. Raise it clear of the basket before transferring toward the remaining back-right cup.
Carry the final egg toward the holder and gently incline the wrist for a front approach to the back cup, avoiding the upright lid.
Position the retained last egg above the back-right cup with the wrist inclined in front of the lid; then reassess alignment for descent.
Lower toward the final cup while drawing the wrist slightly forward of the upright lid, compensating with a small inclination to keep the egg aligned.
All four eggs are now visible in the holder and the fingers are empty. Open and lift away from the lid, preparing a clear approach to close it.
Move the closed left fingertips above the lid's upper edge, approaching from behind while keeping clear of all four seated eggs.
Lower the closed fingertips just behind the lid's upper edge, centering them before pushing the lid toward the holder.
Contact the upper edge with the closed fingertips and gently push the lid forward and downward toward the seated eggs.
The lid has begun to tip. Continue a gentle forward-and-down arc with the closed fingertips, monitoring contact and avoiding the eggs.
Continue following the lid downward and toward the front of the holder with small closed-finger motions.
The lid now covers the holder. Lift clear, open the left fingers, and begin returning home while correcting the parked right arm's small drift.
The closed lid remains in place. Retract the left arm toward its own home workspace while gradually restoring the home wrist orientation.
